subject: recount-hwk.25 landed: the spec's join key does not resolve for pact worktrees
body:
docs/format-notes.md is committed on wt/formatnotes (e13629b). One finding needs a spec decision before recount-hwk.29 (claude_code connector) and whatever bead owns the join.

The spec's join is: invoked_from -> worktree path -> session cwd. Measured on this machine, session `cwd` is the Claude Code PROCESS cwd. A pact fleet agent enters wt/<agent> with a bash `cd`, so the process cwd never moves. Proof: my own transcript is ~/.claude/projects/-home-chussenot-Documents-recount/cd7c75eb-.../subagents/agent-a34d3106441943c34.jsonl and every cwd line in it says /home/chussenot/Documents/recount, not .../wt/formatnotes. All fleet agents of one run share one cwd and one project directory, so cwd cannot separate siblings.

Only Claude Code's own /worktree feature (.claude/worktrees/<name>) relocates cwd, and it also emits a `worktree-state` line carrying worktreePath/worktreeName/worktreeBranch. 420 such lines in the corpus.

Practical consequence: the transcript-mention signal (PACT_AGENT name / bead id) is not a tiebreaker, it is the primary key for pact-style worktrees, alongside the <agent>.meta.json `description` sidecar (mine reads "W0 empirical format-notes bead"). cwd stays useful only to select candidate sessions at repo level. Section 4.3 of format-notes.md has the detail and the counts.

Second thing worth knowing early: the directory-name encoding is lossy and non-injective ( / . _ + and - all encode to - ), so --repo must encode candidate paths forward and never decode a directory name. Section 1.3.

subject: candidates() recurses; generic_jsonl's doc says it does not walk subdirectories
body:
recount-hwk.24 is done (4924322). candidates() now recurses over directory entries, as the wave-0 notes require for the nested <session-uuid>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl shape (604 of 871 files).

Seam nit, no signature change: src/connector/generic_jsonl.rs's module doc promises 'does not walk subdirectories'. Anything built on the shared candidates() now does. Over a flat dir of *.jsonl — the layout that connector describes — recursion is a no-op, so nothing breaks; the docs only disagree on a tree generic_jsonl was never pointed at. I noted it in candidates()' doc rather than editing a file I do not own. If you want generic_jsonl to be genuinely non-recursive it needs its own one-level listing, not the shared function — say so and I will add a candidates_flat(), but I think the right fix is one word in that module doc.

Nothing else wrong with the seam: the trait, the Vec-not-Result tolerance contract, and the dirs+window argument shape all held up unchanged.

subject: recount-hwk.30: non-git --repo is now an error (skeleton doc said otherwise)
body:
recount-hwk.30 is committed on wt/worktree (1c0db50). One deliberate deviation from the skeleton's published doc comment, flagged because other beads may read it:

The skeleton's doc on worktrees() said "A repo that is not a git repository is not an error: it is treated as a single directory with no linked worktrees, so sessions --repo /some/dir still works." My brief said "A --repo that is not a git repo must be a clean error, not a panic." I followed the brief: worktrees() returns Err("--repo <path> is not a git repository: <git stderr>"), and I rewrote that paragraph to say so. Signatures are unchanged, so join/sessions/doctor still compile; only the runtime behaviour of a non-repo --repo differs. Say the word before the wave barrier if you want the tolerant version back — it is a two-line change.

Two other things the consumers should know:
1. worktrees() names the main checkout "main", not by its directory, because that is what invoked_from says in .pact/events.jsonl (9 events).
2. session_dirs() deduplicates by encoded name, because encode() is not injective and two checkouts can share one directory.
